intentional_change_vs_pre_change_baselin.method: the pre-picker commit cb3fad0 and the deployed 1cf9b6d rendered side by side on identical (empty) local data; element-scoped captures
intentional_change_vs_pre_change_baselin.reading: steps ١ and ٢ are pixel-identical (0.0000%) at all three viewports and the composer step keeps its width — the delta is an additive block in step ٣ only

measured.instrument_correction: the first two pixel runs reported 0.0000% at 1024x768 and 390x844. That was an artifact of QA's own instrument: a blanket page.route interceptor delayed /admin/templates past a fixed wait, and the dashboard scrolls inside an inner container (measured docScrollH == docClientH with 2-3 inner scrollers), so full_page captured only the top region. Re-run with an explicit readiness wait and element-scoped captures; the corrected numbers are the ones recorded here.

concerns_non_blocking.finding: canonicalTitle maps a model-proposed button title by SUBSTRING containment, so a negated proposal is inverted into its opposite intent at the emit site.
concerns_non_blocking.impact: the label the customer sees is silently rewritten: «لست مهتمًا بالعرض التجاري» and «لا أريد العرض التجاري» both become commercial titles. Reachable only when the model composes a negated title (customer input still matches exactly), so it is a latent risk, not an observed production defect. «ليس الآن شكرًا» → «ليس الآن» resolves correctly.
concerns_non_blocking.suggested_check: reject a proposal containing a negation particle before the substring match

concerns_non_blocking.finding: 4 of the 82 assertions cannot fail: the 'canonical(«X») is routable' loop derives its EXPECTED value from the ACTUAL (`c ? true : "rejected"`).

measured.verdict: CANNOT FAIL — the expectation is derived from the actual; a total canonicalisation regression still passes

concerns_non_blocking.impact: with canonicalTitle mutated to always return undefined, those 4 assertions still report 4/4 pass. The gate would not catch a total canonicalisation regression through those cases (the two explicit cases on lines 126-129 would still catch it).

concerns_non_blocking.finding: the commit under test moved twice during this gate run: the brief named 5f38d56, then f9a51f0, and the artifact actually deployed is 1cf9b6d.

measured.detection: QA detected working-tree drift mid-run (four source files modified between 19:17 and 19:21) and re-pinned to clean worktrees rather than testing the mutable tree

concerns_non_blocking.impact: no product impact — f9a51f0 and 1cf9b6d are byte-identical in src/agent.ts, src/templates.ts, src/index.ts, scripts/check-buttons.mjs and package.json, so the contract evidence binds to both; only src/dashboard.ts differs. Recorded so the SHA on this bundle is not read as the SHA that was reviewed.

method_limits: Wire behaviour is NOT proven: no message was sent to WhatsApp, so Gupshup's own acceptance of these button titles (including the 20-char rule and Arabic rendering on a device) remains unverified by this gate. The 131009 cap is enforced in code and asserted at boot; that is a code claim, not a wire claim.

Moves 2 and 3 of the founder sequence are model turns. The LLM was not called (no key on the QA instance); what was measured is the OBJECTIVE the model would be given, executed from the real sliced source. Model output quality is not covered.

The end-to-end rung-one bodies read «الخدمة» rather than a service name because the QA instance runs memory-only with no product assets; the service-named variant is covered by check-buttons against the compiled rungOne().

Visual baselines are the reference render recorded for THIS commit (permitted by the playbook when a legacy approval is advanced); the pre-change delta is reported separately with real ratios rather than being forced under the 1% threshold.
